channel.title: Satej Chaudhari — Writeups
channel.description: Offensive-security writeups: HackTheBox, Vulnhub, and lab builds.

item.title: HackTheBox: MonitorFour
item.description: A Cacti vhost, a leaked .env and an IDOR expose user hashes; CVE-2025-24367 gives an in-container shell; and an exposed Docker Engine API on the host is abused to escape to root.

item.title: HackTheBox: Nunchucks
item.description: A Nunjucks server-side template injection behind a vhost gives a reverse shell, and a Perl setuid capability combined with a weak AppArmor profile escalates to root.

item.title: HackTheBox: BabyTwo
item.description: A guest-readable share leaks a user list, a username=password spray gets a foothold, a writable SYSVOL logon script catches a user, and a BloodHound-guided ACL to GPO abuse chain reaches Domain Admin.

item.title: HackTheBox: ReDelegate
item.description: Anonymous FTP yields a KeePass database cracked with a hint-built wordlist; secrets spray into MSSQL and AD; a ForceChangePassword ACL takes over a user; and SeEnableDelegationPrivilege plus GenericAll on a computer is abused for constrained delegation with protocol transition to DCSync the domain.

item.title: HackTheBox: Rebound
item.description: To the user flag — a RID-brute user list feeds a no-pre-auth Kerberoast, a cracked service ticket is reused, and a BloodHound chain of group self-add and forced ACL inheritance resets a service account for the user flag.

item.title: A Six-Segment IDS Lab with Linux Namespaces & Suricata
item.description: Building an isolated six-segment network from Linux namespaces, forcing every packet through an inline Suricata sensor, and writing per-subnet rules that detect and block SQL injection, anonymous FTP, SSH brute force, LDAP honeypot enumeration, and password spraying.

item.title: Setting Up Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS)
item.description: A step-by-step build of an AD lab: installing the AD DS role, promoting a domain controller for a new forest, creating users, joining a client, and importing and linking the Windows 11 security-baseline GPO.

item.title: OSINT From a Single Domain: A Red Team Methodology
item.description: A phase-by-phase OSINT workflow for an authorised red team engagement that starts with nothing but a domain name.

item.title: Vintage: HackTheBox
item.description: Writeup for a Active Directory machine on HackTheBox.

item.title: Vulnhub: Venom
item.description: A hash hidden in page source, an FTP foothold, a chain of encoded clues to a Subrion CMS 4.2.1 login, a public CMS exploit for the shell, and a wide-open sudo rule for root.

item.title: Vulnhub: Matrix 1
item.description: A base64-then-Brainfuck clue chain leaks a partial SSH password, crunch and hydra finish it, a vi restricted-shell escape gives a real shell, and a passwordless sudo rule gives root.

item.title: Vulnhub: Matrix 2
item.description: A robots.txt hint and an unauthenticated POST leak usernames, a cracked .htpasswd hash and a steghide-hidden password lead in, and a sudo-runnable gawk binary gives root.

item.title: Vulnhub: Matrix 3
item.description: A white-rabbit directory maze hides a crackable hash, a Windows binary reversed in Ghidra leaks SSH credentials, and two chained sudo rules walk the way to root.

item.title: Vulnhub: Aragog (HackingHP)
item.description: A vulnerable WordPress File Manager plugin for the foothold, database credentials that crack a user's WordPress hash, and a writable root-run backup script for the root shell.

item.title: Vulnhub: Grotesque 1
item.description: To the user flag — a WordPress password that is the MD5 of a song lyric, a reverse shell planted in the theme's 404.php, and credential reuse from wp-config.php to reach user.txt.
